extracted.intended_audience: Christian parents, masters, and youth seeking moral/religious instruction (17th-century English context)
extracted.subtask_short: moral guidance on swearing and upbringing
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive dialogue giving moral rules and illustrative examples about the sins of swearing, cursing, drunkenness, and the proper responsibilities of masters/parents in raising apprentices and youth. Emphasises causes, signs, and consequences of vice and practical safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sinfulness of unnecessary swearing
rubrics_metrics.description: “A man may say, The Lord liveth, and that is true, and yet in so saying, swear falsly; because he sweareth vainly, needlesly, and without a ground. To swear groundedly and necessarily... that is tolerated of the Word: but this was none of Mr. Badmans swearing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swearing even to a truth can be sinful when done vainly, needlessly, or without ground. Only when swearing is grounded and necessary (e.g., called thereto of God) is it tolerated. Anti-pattern: swearing casually to emphasize or to boast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing to confirm jests and lies is a grave sin
rubrics_metrics.description: Swear to confirm their Jests and Lies; and as they think, the better to beautifie their foolish talking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calling God to witness a lie or a jest is equated with lying, killing, stealing, adultery and considered worthy of punishment. Example: those who tell tales and then swear by God they are true are committing a high affront to God's holiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and moral weight of cursing
rubrics_metrics.description: “To Curse profanely, it is to sentence another or our self, for, or to evil: or to wish that some evil might happen to the person or thing under the Curse, unjustly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cursing includes (a) wrongfully sentencing another to evil (unjust accusation) and (b) wishing that evil befall someone. Both are grievous sins illustrated by biblical examples (Shimei, Job). Anti-patterns: using curses as casual expletives or to vent anger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cursing oneself as a form of damnatory wish
rubrics_metrics.description: He would also as often wish a Curse to himself, saying, Would I might be hanged, or burned, or that the Devil might fetch me... they rather curse than swear; yea, curse themselves, and that with a Wish that Damnation might light upon themselves;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-directed curses (wishing damnation upon oneself) are condemned as extremely dangerous; such wishes are presented as precursors to divine judgement if unrepented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cursing dishonours God through His image
rubrics_metrics.description: Man is Gods Image, and to curse wickedly the Image of God, is to curse God himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because humans are made in God's image, to curse or condemn a neighbour is to affront God. Argument used to show the seriousness of cursing: it's not merely social harm but sacrilegious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots/causes of swearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Swearing... flows from that daring Boldness that biddeth defiance to the Law... flows sometimes from hellish Rage... from the promptings of the spirit of the Devil within them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated causes: (1) devilish promptings, (2) hellish rage, (3) daring boldness/defiance of law, (4) desire to seem valiant, (5) to deceive/overcome others, (6) to get gain. Use these as diagnostics for diagnosing why someone swears and to target correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical warning against employing common swearers
rubrics_metrics.description: no Buyer should lay out one farthing with him that is a common Swearer in his Calling; especially with such an Oath-master that endeavoureth to swear away his commodity to another, and that would swear his Chapmans money into his own pocket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swearers are unreliable and morally compromised in business; practical advice: avoid doing business with habitual swearers or those who use oaths to commit fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of cursing
rubrics_metrics.description: This evil of Cursing ariseth, in general, from the desperate wickedness of the heart, but particularly from... 1. Envie... 2. Pride... 3. Scorn and contempt of others... 4. desperate Madness (for a man to curse himself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to diagnose tendencies toward cursing; corrective measures should address envy, pride, contempt, and madness/desperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing and cursing as sins against the light of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: To curse another, and to swear vainly and falsly, are sins against the Light of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: natural reason condemns these practices—one would not wish to be treated so, nor to call God to witness falsehood—so they violate both divine and natural law. Use this to persuade those who appeal to natural reason rather than scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of exempla (divine judgments) as deterrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Wise presents multiple examples of divine judgement (Dorothy Mately, Ned, N. P. at Wimbleton) as demonstrations of God's punishment for swearing and cursing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories of sudden death, possession, and righteous judgement are offered as warnings to frighten and deter. Guidance: employ vivid exempla when urging repentance; anti-pattern: dismissing anecdotes as mere superstition without moral lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: avoid overworking apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: If he be not moderate in the use of his Apprentice; if he drives him beyond his strength; if he holds him to work at unseasonable hours; if he will not allow him convenient time to read the Word, to Pray, &c. This is the way to destroy him;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masters should allow reasonable hours and time for spiritual practices; excessive labour in youth destroys tender spiritual beginnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: guard reading material in the household
rubrics_metrics.description: If he suffers his house to be scattered with profane and wicked Books... such as tend to corrupt, and pervert the Doctrine of Faith and Holiness. All these things will eat as doth a canker, and will quickly spoil... good beginnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control access to corrupting literature; provide wholesome books. Anti-pattern: tolerating romances, ribaldry, and doctrinal perversions in the home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: avoid keeping corrupted servants
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be a mixture of Servants, that is, if some very bad be in the same place, that’s a way also to undo such tender Lads;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A master should not employ openly bad servants whose speech and conduct will influence apprentices; peer environment matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: consistency between public and private life
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Master have one Guise for abroad, and another for home; that is, if his Religion hangs by in his house as his Cloak does... Children make a greater inspection into the Lives of Fathers, Masters, &c. than oft-times they are aware of: And therefore should Masters be carefull, else they may soon destroy good beginnings in their Servants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypocrisy undermines teaching; masters must live consistently so apprentices do not stumble at double standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: fair dealing in trade
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Master be unconscionable in his Dealing, and trades with lying words... or if he seeks after unreasonable gain... his servant sees it, and it is enough to undo him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unethical business practices model dishonesty; masters must conduct trade honestly to form moral apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs an apprentice rejects good instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: For good Books, they might lie in his Masters house till they rotted for him... For good Instruction, he liked that, much as he liked good books; his care was to hear but little thereof... his way was, when come into the place of hearing, to sit down in some corner, and then to fall fast asleep... Or else to fix his adulterous eyes upon some beautifull Object... Or... whispering, gigling, and playing with them, till such time as Sermon was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral signs: neglecting good books, hating rebuke, sleeping, flirting, whispering during sermons. These are diagnostics to identify and correct spiritual indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perils of bad companionship
rubrics_metrics.description: Those companions were given to Uncleanness, Drunkenness, Purloining... they taught him to adde to his sin, much of like kind... he became a Frequenter of Taverns and Tippling-houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being given to vile companions accelerates moral ruin; avoid company that specializes in uncleanness, drunkenness, theft. Preventative: control friendships and associations for youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four practical harms of drunkenness
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four things... 1. It greatly tendeth to impoverish and beggar a man... 2. This sin of Drunkenness, it bringeth upon the Body, many, great, and incurable Diseases... 3. Drunkenness, is a sin that is often times attended with abundance of other evils... 4. By Drunkenness, Men do often times shorten their dayes;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these concrete consequences (poverty, disease, attendant evils, early death) as persuasive arguments against drinking. Also spiritual consequence: drunkenness prepares men for 'everlasting burnings' and makes conversion unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness as spiritual stupor preventing repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: It so stupifies and besotts the soul, that a man that is far gone in Drunkenness, is hardly ever recovered to God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: urgent intervention is needed early; it's rare for an old drunkard to be converted. Anti-pattern: assuming habitual drunkards will easily reform without strong measures.
